annotation.title_clean: Directive 2009/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 June 2009 on the safety of toys
annotation.title_en: Directive 2009/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 June 2009 on the safety of toys
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, L 170/1
annotation.summary_en: EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC sets essential safety requirements for toys for children under 14, obligations for manufacturers, importers and distributors, CE marking, conformity assessment via harmonised standards or EC-type examination, notified bodies, and market surveillance. It has no AI-specific content; relevance to robotics is limited to toys.
key_provisions_or_claims: Toys must not jeopardise safety or health when used as intended or foreseeably, bearing in mind children's behaviour.
Manufacturers must perform hazard analysis, technical documentation, EC declaration of conformity and CE marking.
Conformity via harmonised standards (internal production control) or EC-type examination by notified bodies.
Strict chemical limits, including a ban on CMR substances, with limited derogations.
Member States must run market surveillance and set effective, proportionate, dissuasive penalties.
